title: Homeward
summary: A source-grounded discharge system that turns hospital instructions into a persistent recovery plan with exact citations, deterministic next steps, specialist assistance, care-team review, and safely retryable reminders.
landingDeck: Homeward makes a discharge record operational: patients can see what to do next and why, carry missing details into clarification, ask from their own sources, request human help, and approve a dated reminder without giving the agent authority over clinical instructions or side effects.
landingHighlights: Models reviewed, unreviewed, missing, paused, historical, completed, and clarification states so uncertainty remains visible across the patient and care-team workflow.
Constrains four patient-and-role-scoped specialists to server-enforced MCP tool inventories while deterministic services retain approval, dates, reminders, escalation, and emergency controls.
Passed 59 backend and contract tests, four React DOM journeys, a production build, and 32/32 deterministic guardrail cases in the recorded integrated verification.
problem: Discharge instructions arrive when patients and caregivers are tired, anxious, and newly responsible for coordinating follow-up, documents, recovery checks, laboratory questions, warning signs, and dates. Missing or conflicting details can become dangerous when a summary quietly turns uncertainty into a confident instruction.
approach: Homeward converts the discharge record into typed recovery tasks with exact source references, explicit date provenance, durable clarification state, deterministic next-step selection, patient-scoped lexical search, role-bounded specialist assistance, care-team review, and approval-controlled reminder execution.
output: A React 19 and Express 5 product with SQLite persistence, four TrueForge and MCP specialist roles, patient and care-team workspaces, imported-document review, source-linked summaries, deterministic guidance, idempotent calendar-file creation, immutable audit history, and recorded multi-layer verification.

methodology.evaluation: At commit 456b4a7, recorded verification covers 59 backend and contract tests, four React DOM journeys, a production build, 32/32 deterministic guardrail cases, real MCP exchanges, and mocked native TrueForge sessions across retrieval, routing, approval, revision conflicts, reference validation, response loss, retry, and recovery.
methodology.boundary: The evaluated environment uses fictional discharge instructions and synthetic Synthea history; the product demonstrates workflow authority and failure containment while clinical outcomes and authenticated healthcare deployment remain separate validation programs.

role: I conceived and led Homeward's product direction; defined the patient journey, feature set, team responsibilities, and delivery plan; designed and built the product experience and much of the UI; implemented the backend, audited discharge-review workflow, grounded specialist-agent system, deterministic guidance, structured reference validation, persistence, revision and idempotency controls, and associated tests; created the synthetic patient dataset and Synthea integration; and authored the comprehensive product and technical documentation.

pageSections.title: Homeward turns discharge paperwork into a source-linked plan for recovering at home
pageSections.description: A patient can see the next recorded step, inspect the exact instruction behind it, carry missing details into clarification, ask questions from the saved record, request care-team help, and approve a dated reminder through one continuous workflow.
pageSections.context: The product keeps ready tasks, items needing attention, reported completion, help requests, imported passages, and historical context visible as distinct states.

pageSections.title: Uncertainty remains operational instead of being softened into confident prose
pageSections.markdown:
The primary Alex Morgan journey begins with four concrete tasks: arrange a follow-up visit, gather the required paperwork, complete a dated recovery check-in, and clarify a laboratory instruction whose test and date are absent. Homeward does not fill those gaps. The clarification state follows the item through the patient workspace, source search, saved-record summary, help flow, care-team review, and reminder eligibility checks.

The next-step selector considers pending, unpaused tasks with valid source references and recorded dates. It orders eligible tasks by date and labels the result as scheduling guidance. Completed, rejected, unreviewed, help-paused, historical, and clarification items remain visible in their own states. The dashboard and the question **What is my next step?** consume the same guidance object, keeping the visual recommendation and conversational response aligned.

Every recovery task carries a document ID, section ID, and exact quote. Dates retain their origin: reviewed discharge source, human clarification, or legacy plan entry. Relative language is converted only when the workflow has adequate evidence; an unknown deadline remains empty, preventing a convenient reminder from turning ambiguity into an invented care instruction.

pageSections.title: The patient sees the next step, its source, its owner, and what still needs clarification
pageSections.description: The recovery view makes task state and provenance visible together, so the patient can distinguish an actionable instruction from an imported passage, historical record, unresolved question, or item paused for care-team help.
pageSections.caption: The fictional patient environment supports deterministic evaluation of successful actions, missing details, review decisions, stale approvals, and recoverable failures.

pageSections.title: The workflow carries a question from the record to a verified patient action
pageSections.description: Read-only guidance remains responsive while clinical wording, dates, approvals, and side effects stay under deterministic application control.

items.label: Resolve
items.title: Load the bound patient and current plan
items.body: Read the patient's tasks, sources, review status, help state, dates, completion reports, and current plan revision from SQLite.

items.label: Guide
items.title: Select the next valid recorded step
items.body: Apply deterministic eligibility and ordering rules, then return the task, owner, date, source quote, and reason it is next.

items.label: Assist
items.title: Search sources or route to a bounded specialist
items.body: Use lexical search and saved-record summaries directly, or send one request to the coordinator, summarizer, questions, or reminders role with a patient-specific tool inventory.

items.label: Review
items.title: Validate references and request human judgment
items.body: Resolve every selected task, source, and action against the current patient snapshot; send unclear instructions to the local care-team workspace and show consequential proposals before approval.

items.label: Act
items.title: Execute once and recover visibly
items.body: Bind the approved action to the task revision and source, create the local calendar artifact once, retain the receipt, and return the same result when a lost response is retried.

pageSections.title: Four roles receive different tools because their authority is genuinely different
pageSections.description: The deterministic router selects one role from explicit intent or request language. Each role has a native AgentSpec, a patient-and-role-scoped MCP endpoint, and a server-enforced tool inventory.

items.label: Coordinator
items.title: Organize plan work without approving it
items.body: Read the patient snapshot, inspect guidance, and propose a task-level coordination step while leaving instruction approval and clinical wording to deterministic services and human review.

items.label: Summarizer
items.title: Explain the saved discharge record
items.body: Read summaries and source passages, organize ready tasks and unresolved items, and return patient-facing structure without receiving reminder-execution tools.

items.label: Questions
items.title: Answer from patient-bound sources
items.body: Search exact passages and select source references for ordinary discharge questions; the backend reconstructs the response from stored text after validating patient scope and plan revision.

items.label: Reminders
items.title: Prepare an eligible reminder
items.body: Inspect a known dated task, propose a reminder, and execute only a reminder already approved through Homeward's UI and API. No agent receives an approval tool.

pageSections.title: The model selects references; the application decides what those references are allowed to mean

items.label: Identity
items.title: Every tool call is patient-bound
items.body: MCP endpoints and store operations resolve one patient and role. Foreign, fabricated, malformed, or stale identifiers are rejected before they can affect the plan.

items.label: Language
items.title: Stored records supply the clinical wording
items.body: Structured model output selects source, task, and action identifiers plus an optional allowlisted education topic. The backend reconstructs exact text from current records.

items.label: Approval
items.title: Homeward owns consequential decisions
items.body: Agents cannot approve instructions, resolve help, modify medication, book appointments, send messages, or dispatch emergency care. Human-facing UI and API flows retain those controls.

items.label: Freshness
items.title: Plan changes invalidate prior authority
items.body: Optimistic revisions prevent reviewers from overwriting newer decisions, and action fingerprints bind reminders to the exact task revision, source, instruction, and date.

pageSections.title: Imported records become searchable evidence before they become actionable instructions
pageSections.markdown:
Homeward accepts pasted text, TXT or Markdown, and text-based PDFs, divides them into searchable passages, and labels the resulting material unreviewed. A patient or specialist can retrieve an exact passage and propose it for review. The care-team workspace can confirm, clarify, or reject the passage while retaining the original citation and the before-and-after task snapshots in immutable audit history.

Historical Synthea records remain distinct from authored discharge instructions, imported passages, human clarifications, and general education. Provenance reaches the source file, row, fields, and hash, allowing the product to use realistic longitudinal context without treating a historical medication record as a current discharge order.

An open help request pauses completion and reminder execution for the affected task. The care-team operator can respond or resolve the conversation, but resolving a help request does not silently approve an instruction or create a missing deadline. This separation makes uncertainty visible to both sides of the workflow.

pageSections.title: The reminder workflow demonstrates approval, stale-state rejection, and idempotent recovery

items.label: Check
items.title: Require a reviewed task with a known date
items.body: Block proposals for unresolved, unreviewed, help-paused, historical, completed, or undated instructions.

items.label: Propose
items.title: Show the exact reminder before execution
items.body: Display the task, recorded date, source instruction, responsible party, and action fingerprint in the patient workflow.

items.label: Approve
items.title: Use a separate Homeward decision
items.body: Approve or decline through the product's UI and API; the agent cannot grant its own authority.

items.label: Create
items.title: Generate one local calendar artifact
items.body: Create a local .ics file and execution receipt without claiming an appointment booking, sent message, or background notification.

items.label: Retry
items.title: Return the original receipt after response loss
items.body: If storage succeeds and the response is lost, a retry resolves the idempotency key and returns the first result instead of duplicating the reminder.

pageSections.title: Escalation, education, and emergency access remain independent from agent readiness

items.label: Care team
items.title: Unclear instructions create a durable help item
items.body: The local operator sees the patient, task, source, question, and history, and can respond without silently changing the underlying discharge instruction.

items.label: Education
items.title: General information stays separate from the care plan
items.body: Fixed-topic MedlinePlus lookups return allowlisted links, cache successful results, send no patient identifiers, and cannot modify tasks or dates.

items.label: Emergency
items.title: The patient controls the emergency call
items.body: A persistent US-demo tel:911 control bypasses the agent and lets the user's device initiate the call directly.

items.label: Fallback
items.title: Saved records remain useful during provider failure
items.body: Deterministic next-step guidance, lexical source search, summaries, citations, and care-team workflows continue to operate when model execution is unavailable.

pageSections.title: The evaluation targets the transitions where polished demos hide risk
pageSections.markdown:
The implementation followed explicit contracts for discharge review, next-step selection, source trust, role capabilities, approval, and live evaluation. Shared scenario functions serve both the domain tests and evaluation runner, reducing the chance that presentation evidence exercises a different path from the product.

Critical transitions are checked at multiple layers: store invariants, HTTP behavior, real MCP client exchanges, mocked TrueForge sessions and structured output, React DOM journeys, and a production-browser path with an isolated SQLite database. The live scenario matrix names the expected answer, required sources, allowed and prohibited tools, expected state change, and failure category.

The evaluation includes missing laboratory details, conflicting uploads, cross-patient requests, historical dosage overreach, approval bypass, prompt injection inside a document, repeated reminder proposals, open help requests, tool failure, and runtime outage. Live execution is opt-in, request-capped, budget-referenced, and configured to stop on provider errors. Automated checks verify controls and state; human review remains the authority for answer quality.

pageSections.title: Homeward reduces coordination burden while keeping the record and authority visible

items.label: Patients
items.title: See what to do next and where it came from
items.body: The recovery plan combines task state, owner, date, source quote, open question, help status, and reminder state in one workflow.

items.label: Caregivers
items.title: Coordinate without rewriting the discharge record
items.body: Responsibility and source references travel with each item, while missing details remain explicit instead of becoming informal family interpretations.

items.label: Care teams
items.title: Receive patient-scoped, source-linked clarification requests
items.body: The review workspace shows the instruction, patient question, activity history, plan revision, and prior decision state required for a defensible response.

items.label: Product teams
items.title: Separate helpful assistance from workflow authority
items.body: Role capabilities, reference validation, human approval, idempotency, audit events, and fallback behavior form a reusable pattern for consequential agent products.

pageSections.title: A deeply tested reference implementation for post-discharge coordination
pageSections.markdown:
Homeward implements the patient and care-team experience, source and date provenance, deterministic guidance, imported-record review, four role-scoped specialists, human-controlled approval, local reminder artifacts, stale-action rejection, idempotent recovery, education lookup, emergency access, and multi-layer evaluation.

The evaluated environment uses fictional discharge material and synthetic Synthea history. Clinical outcomes, protected-health-information deployment, authenticated provider integrations, and regulatory validation remain separate healthcare delivery programs.
